en: Taal Volcano contains Vulcan Point, a small island situated inside a crater lake located on Volcano Island within Taal Lake.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan is so massive that it features a full navigable underground waterfall inside its extensive cave system.
Laguna de Bay is the largest lake in the Philippines and is distinctly shaped like the letter W when viewed from above.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a UNESCO World Heritage site situated entirely in the open ocean, hundreds of kilometers from the nearest mainland.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 symmetrical cone-shaped hills that famously turn brown during the dry summer season.
Baguio City is called the Summer Capital of the Philippines because its high mountain elevation keeps its average temperature comfortably below 20 degrees Celsius.
The Philippine Trench in the Pacific Ocean reaches a depth of over 10,500 meters, making it one of the deepest oceanic trenches on Earth.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao were carved into the steep mountains by indigenous people over 2,000 years ago using mostly hand tools.
Mount Mayon in Albay is globally famous for possessing the most perfect natural cone shape among all active volcanoes in the world.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching approximately 505 kilometers through the Cagayan Valley in northern Luzon.
Donsol in Sorsogon is known as the Whale Shark Capital of the Philippines because it hosts a massive annual gathering of gentle giant butanding.
The San Juanico Bridge physically connects the islands of Leyte and Samar, making it the longest bridge in the Philippines at over two kilometers.
